meta.magnitudes: mag = {levels, top}. Apply log10 'levels' times to reach a value 'top' in [1,10). Compare by levels, then top. Entries without a mag are in a growth-class tier; their order inside the tier is only the source's listing order.

orderBasis.source-order: Placed by the source's listing; size not given.
orderBasis.tier-source-order: Inside its growth class, in the Googology Wiki listing order.
orderBasis.anchored-to-neighbour: Placed next to the entry before it in the Bowers checklist.

tiers.label: 10↑↑↑3 up to the start of the omega levels
tiers.note: Reordered by arithmetic where the definitions allow (for example Giggolplex sits between Tria-taxis and Tetra-taxis, and Folkman's number below Googol-3-flex); the wiki lists this class loosely.

tiers.label: Iterated Cantor normal form level (up to epsilon_0)
Bachmann's collapsing level, up to TREE(3)

series.rule: The n-th name stands for 10^(3n+3). n=1 is million.
series.comparison: Magnitude of term n is mag(10^(3n+3)); merge it with 'numbers' using each entry's 'mag'.

valueKinds.pow10: 10^exponent; exponent is a string or a nested value.

scopeNotes: Compound English names (twenty-one, one hundred five) are not listed; only single-word names are.
-illion names are a rule (see series), complete up to a googolplex. Above that, only the named landmarks listed here exist; the Conway-Wechsler rule keeps naming larger n forever, so there is no top.
The googology community has never agreed a total order for the largest numbers. Tier entries are ordered by class, then by source listing.
Numbers below 2 (zero, one, googolminex) are not listed.

excluded.name: Busy Beaver numbers other than the named one
excluded.reason: Named by function BB(n), not by a number name.

excluded.name: Real-world quantities (Planck volumes, largest known prime, Leviathan number)
excluded.reason: Descriptions, not names; or values not verified.
